summary: In this fiction excerpt (Book 2, part 18), the narrator races through Los Angeles traffic with Courtney, driving recklessly over curbs and through lights to reach Anton's garage, which is engulfed in a massive fire. The narrator sees the building collapsing and, after rapid calculations, concludes that nobody could have escaped. They flee the scene to avoid traffic cameras and police, and Courtney asks if the people inside are dead, to which the narrator answers yes, leaving the narrator wondering whether the disaster is their fault. The passage ends mid-thought as the narrator counts the hours since first contacting Anton.
one_line: Fiction excerpt: the narrator and Courtney race to Anton's garage in LA, find it burning, and conclude no one survived.
key_facts: The narrator tore back along the street and dove toward the car, with boots pounding against the asphalt.
The narrator drove through Los Angeles traffic by skidding between lanes and popping the wheels up over the curb to go down a sidewalk.
Courtney sat in the passenger seat, bracing herself against the dashboard while the car sped through the city.
When the car reached the last corner before Anton's garage, a block away, the narrator braked hard, sending Courtney tumbling against the dash.
Anton's building was described as a roaring inferno, with flames towering into the sky and black smoke rolling over the street.
The narrator felt the heat slam into them even at a block's distance, describing it as an oppressive wall of blistering air.
The building was collapsing in on itself, with its walls and roof folding in massive flares of sparks.
The narrator ran the timing numbers three different ways and concluded that even with the most generous estimates, nobody had made it out.
The narrator returned to the car, whose door metal was already warm, and made a U-turn to drive back the way they came.
The narrator planned to ditch the car a block or two away in case traffic cameras had captured the vehicular stunts.
Courtney asked timidly, "Did they...are they..." and the narrator answered, "Dead."
The narrator said "I'm sure" when Courtney asked if they were sure.
The narrator wondered whether the deaths were Courtney's fault or their own.
The narrator had contacted Anton a little over five hours before this scene.
Traffic going into the city had delayed the narrator for a good chunk of time before they headed straight to Anton's garage.
